headline: 3-bed mid-terrace BRR, Bolton BL3, £95k
summary: A three-bedroom mid-terrace in Bolton BL3 offered at £95,000 against a claimed current value of £120,000. The sourcer proposes a light-to-medium refurb of £15,000 (kitchen, bathroom, decoration) with a post-works value of £145,000 and an achievable rent of £850 per month. The vendor is described as a landlord exiting the market and wanting a quick sale. No comparables, photos or survey were included.
strategy_rationale: Pitched on the basis of buying below value, refurbishing and refinancing to pull most of the cash back out.

property.condition: Dated but habitable; needs new kitchen, bathroom and full redecoration according to the sourcer.

financials.exit_strategy: Refinance onto a BTL mortgage at 75% LTV and hold

qualitative.notes: BL3 has solid rental demand for family lets. The £145k end value is a 21% uplift on a £15k refurb, which is optimistic without comparables. Refurb budget looks thin if the electrics or roof need attention. No survey, photos or floor plan were provided.

red_flags: Post-works value of £145,000 is not supported by any comparables.
£15,000 refurb budget for kitchen, bathroom and full redecoration leaves no contingency.
missing_information: Sold comparables for the street or immediate area
Photos, floor plan and EPC certificate
Itemised refurb quote from a builder
Confirmation of vacant possession and any tenancy history
Council tax band and any Article 4 or selective licensing in BL3
questions_for_sourcer: Which sold comparables support the £145k post-works valuation?
Is the £15k refurb figure from a builder's quote or an estimate, and what does it include?
Has the property been surveyed, and is there any history of damp or roof issues?
Is the £3k sourcing fee payable on exchange or completion, and is it refundable if the deal falls through?
Can you share the full address so I can run my own checks?
verdict: On the sourcer's numbers this is a reasonable BRR that would leave under 20% of the cash in after refinance with a gross yield above 10%. The deal stands or falls on the £145k end value, which is unsupported. Worth a same-day request for comparables and a builder's quote before spending anything on a survey.
